summary_hint: tax year, filing status, taxpayer(s), and the qualifying-income figures (AGI, total income, wages, business net, net rental) alongside the list of schedules filed — what a processor needs to know a return is complete and which income methodology applies without opening the bundle.

typed_core.name: tax_year
typed_core.why: AU-1 (which year's income to compare), IN-12; identity + disambiguator — the year must sit beside every figure or a prior-year return is matched to the current AUS.

typed_core.name: amended_return_indicator
typed_core.why: DT-7 — an amended (1040-X) return changes which figures are authoritative; processor.

typed_core.name: filing_status
typed_core.why: processor — interprets joint vs single income; needed to attribute income to one or two borrowers.

typed_core.name: taxpayer_name
typed_core.why: identity/attribution — ties the return to a borrower (feeds name-consistency); flattened from person.

typed_core.name: spouse_name
typed_core.why: identity — a joint return's second party is often the co-borrower; flattened from person.

typed_core.name: taxpayer_ssn_masked
typed_core.why: PII (pre-masked) — identity/attribution key; already in _PII_FIELDS.
typed_core.prompt_hint: Mask both taxpayer and spouse SSN to last-4; never emit a full SSN anywhere, including reasoning.

typed_core.name: spouse_ssn_masked
typed_core.why: PII (pre-masked) — identity; needs _PII_FIELDS registration.

typed_core.name: home_address
typed_core.why: identity/occupancy — the residence of record is an address signal for OC-3/OC-1; processor. Flattened from address.

typed_core.name: wages_salaries_tips
typed_core.why: AU-1 (documented income vs AUS), DT-7 (documented income factor).

typed_core.name: business_income_or_loss
typed_core.why: AU-1, IN-12 — the 1040 line that Schedule C net flows to; the self-employment signal at summary level.

typed_core.name: total_income
typed_core.why: AU-1, DT-7.

typed_core.name: adjusted_gross_income
typed_core.why: AU-1, DT-7 — the headline qualifying figure.

typed_core.name: total_net_rental_income
typed_core.why: IN-14, OC-3 — the amount that triggers 'rental income detected → require support'.

typed_core.name: taxable_income
typed_core.why: processor; AU-1 cross-check.

typed_core.name: standard_or_itemized_deduction
typed_core.why: processor — itemized vs standard hints at unreimbursed expenses affecting income.

typed_core.name: total_tax
typed_core.why: processor; DT-7 completeness.

typed_core.name: federal_income_tax_withheld
typed_core.why: processor — cross-check against W-2 withholding / wage income.

typed_core.name: total_payments
typed_core.why: processor.

typed_core.name: attached_schedules_and_forms
typed_core.why: DT-7 (documentation inventory), IN-14/OC-3 (is Schedule E present?), IN-12 (is Schedule C / K-1 present?) — the schedule-presence signal. Degraded from string[]; comma-joined.
typed_core.prompt_hint: List schedule identifiers as printed (e.g. 'Schedule C', 'Schedule E', 'Schedule 1', 'K-1') so DT-7 has an inventory.

typed_core.name: return_signed_date
typed_core.why: DT-7 (return executed/documented); processor recency.

typed_core.name: signatures_present
typed_core.why: DT-7 — an unsigned return is an ATR documentation gap. Degraded from signature[] → present/absent.

nested_lists.name: schedule_c
nested_lists.shape_reason: few items (typically 1–3 businesses) so the heavy shape is affordable, and IN-12's add-back methodology audits each figure individually, so each needs its own page/snippet.

fields.name: business_name
fields.why: IN-12 — identify the business the Schedule C reports

fields.name: total_expenses
fields.why: IN-12 — the expense total behind net profit

fields.name: net_profit
fields.why: IN-12, AU-1 — Schedule C net profit is the self-employment income

fields.name: depreciation
fields.why: IN-12 — [RULE FLOOR — absent from catalog] add-back (net profit + depreciation add-back → qualifying income)

fields.name: depletion
fields.why: IN-12 — [RULE FLOOR — absent from catalog] add-back

fields.name: amortization
fields.why: IN-12 — [RULE FLOOR — absent from catalog] add-back

fields.name: business_use_of_home
fields.why: IN-12 — [RULE FLOOR — absent from catalog] add-back

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: a 1040 is a known form; classification handles it — no rule

rejected.name: issuer_name
rejected.reason: not meaningful on a self-/preparer-filed return; no rule

rejected.name: statement_period_start / _end
rejected.reason: a return is not a statement; tax_year covers the period

rejected.name: document_status_or_version, return_version
rejected.reason: amended_return_indicator carries the only status a rule uses

rejected.name: dependents
rejected.reason: household size — no rule reads it; catch-all

rejected.name: tax_exempt/taxable_interest, qualified/ordinary_dividends, capital_gain_or_loss, other_income_schedule1
rejected.reason: not read by any current rule; total_income/AGI cover AU-1/DT-7; catch-all captures the detail

rejected.name: refund_amount, amount_owed, estimated_tax_and_other_payments, estimated_tax_penalty
rejected.reason: no rule; total_tax/total_payments cover the result

rejected.name: direct_deposit_or_payment_account_last4
rejected.reason: restricted PII with no consumer — do not surface

encoding_variations: Tax year appears in the masthead ('2023'), in 'For the year Jan 1–Dec 31, 2023', and sometimes only in the form revision line — must be the return's tax year, not the print/filing year.

Rental income is not a 1040 line — it reaches the 1040 via Schedule E → Schedule 1 line 5. A model must read Schedule E, not search the 1040 face, hence total_net_rental_income is flagged absent-from-catalog.
Business income on the 1040 (Schedule 1 line 3) is net of Schedule C; a loss prints in parentheses/negative.
Amended returns may show 'Amended', check-box, or the 1040-X header; figures then supersede the original.
Money may carry $, commas, and parentheses for negatives.

open_questions.q: More than one nested list. Section 5 budgets one nested list/document, but IN-12 reads K-1 ordinary income/distributions and IN-14/OC-3 read Schedule E rental figures — genuinely repeating and rule-demanded.
options: keep only schedule_c nested, flatten a single Schedule-E total + a single K-1 total into core
retain all three nested lists (schedule_c, schedule_e, k1s) as the existing extractor does
open_questions.recommendation: (b) — the rules read all three; the plumbing already exists. Flag the multi-property / multi-K-1 count as the token-budget risk. GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Schedule C add-back set. IN-12's methodology determines exactly which add-backs count. Included depreciation/depletion/amortization/business-use-of-home as the common set.
options: confirm the authoritative list before build
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the authoritative list before build so the calculator floor is complete. GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): ship the common add-back set (depreciation/depletion/amortization/business-use-of-home).

open_questions.q: total_net_rental_income placement. It is a derived Schedule E roll-up, not a 1040 line.
options: keep it as a typed-core signal for IN-14/OC-3 detection
derive it from the schedule_e nested list instead
open_questions.recommendation: keep the top-level signal so detection does not depend on nested-list plumbing being wired. GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): keep the top-level rental signal (total_net_rental_income).

open_questions.q: home_address masking. Standard sensitivity, but a real home address in the unmasked catch-all was the section 6 incident. Promoted as typed (done) — should it also be _PII_FIELDS-registered?
open_questions.recommendation: Priya decides. GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

notes: The catalog is entirely 1040-summary level; it carries no per-schedule detail. IN-12 (self-employment methodology), IN-14 and OC-3 (rental support) all read Schedule C / E / K-1 figures that do not exist as catalog fields — the primary rule-floor gaps, which live in the nested list(s), not the flat core.

The diff recommends retaining schedule_e (properties + totals) and k1s nested lists (Open Q1), but only schedule_c is field-specified in the Repeating lists section; only schedule_c is emitted here, with schedule_e/k1s carried in the open question.

PII: taxpayer_ssn_masked already registered; spouse_ssn_masked needs _PII_FIELDS registration (pre_masked true) — a joint return prints the spouse SSN in full and left to the catch-all it is stored unmasked.
Ambiguity: tax_year is tagged identity + disambiguator but also serves AU-1/IN-12 as the join key; classified rule (primary consumer) with AU-1/IN-12 in rules.

Ambiguity: home_address is tagged identity/occupancy + processor and cites OC-3/OC-1; classified processor with rules [] so rules_served stays aligned with the 5-rule header (OC-3 is served via total_net_rental_income). PII object left null pending Priya's masking decision (Open Q4), even though it is a real address.
